data: Asteroid · Jupiter Trojan · L5 · Binary secondary

104-km secondary of the Patroclus-Menoetius binary in the L5 Trojan swarm — nearly equal-mass partner to Patroclus, separated by 680 km. Lucy's 2033-03 encounter will be the first close-up of a Trojan binary system, mapping both partners simultaneously.

104-km secondary of the Patroclus-Menoetius binary in the L5 Trojan cloud. Co-orbital with Patroclus at 680-km mutual separation; the pair forms the largest binary system known among the Jupiter Trojans. Lucy encounter 2033-03-02.
Menoetius is Patroclus's binary companion at L5. Their tight binary geometry has kept them dynamically stable for 4.5 billion years.
Five gravitationally-balanced spots in every two-body system where a small spacecraft can hover with almost no fuel — and where most modern deep-space observatories actually live.
